notice: All organizations, inputs, activity and results are synthetic. This proposed workflow is not a connected employer system or measured company performance.
title: A useful signal still needs a reliable delivery path.
intro: A proposed implementation workbench for Sentrion: turn a customer’s account-intelligence use case into a mapped, testable workflow with visible failures and an operator handover.
queueIntro: Each fictional customer has a target CRM field, an update key and an owner. Inspect how a delivery should behave when input is incomplete or a service returns an error.
workbenchIntro: Change the mapping and delivery result. A retry is appropriate for some failures; it cannot repair a missing field or unapproved access.
firstBody: Map the signal to the customer’s intended task, validate required fields and preserve an event key. Classify exceptions and give an operator a clear next action.

fields.label: Required source and target fields mapped
Stable account and event key present

rules.title: Repair the field mapping
rules.next: Missing target fields need a mapping change before another delivery attempt.

rules.title: Preserve a stable event key
rules.next: Without a key the system cannot reliably distinguish a repeated event from a new update.

rules.title: Resolve destination access
rules.next: Confirm the approved destination and permissions with its owner. No credentials are requested in this demo.

rules.title: Skip the duplicate event
rules.next: The event key already has a delivered receipt. Preserve it and do not create a second CRM update.

rules.title: Route authentication to the access owner
rules.next: Retrying the same request does not repair access. Keep the failed event available for a reviewed replay.

rules.title: Quarantine the invalid payload
rules.next: Keep the event key and error details, then correct the mapping before a reviewed replay.

rules.title: Escalate exhausted retries
rules.next: The illustrative three-attempt budget is exhausted. Move the event to an owned exception queue.

rules.title: Schedule a bounded retry
rules.next: Respect the provider response and reuse the original event key. No real request is made.

rules.title: Test the customer’s acceptance criterion
rules.next: A delivered event is not a useful workflow until the receiving team validates the expected behavior.

rules.title: Complete the operator handover
rules.next: Record ownership, expected update behavior and recovery steps before rollout.

ready.title: Ready for operator review
ready.next: Mapping, event identity, access and acceptance are recorded. A customer operator can review the proposed rollout and recovery plan.

records.name: Birch Systems

records.name: Willow Software

metricsTitle: Distinguish delivery, replay and unresolved work.
metricsIntro: Synthetic event outcomes for one fixed run window. A skipped duplicate is a successful safeguard, not a second delivery.
metricsNotes: Use unique event keys as the delivery denominator; separate attempts from events.
A bounded retry budget needs an explicit owner and a terminal state. It must not silently discard work.
Validate missing inputs, field changes, duplicate events and service failures before a real rollout.

experiments.name: Task-first implementation brief
experiments.hypothesis: An agreed customer task helps identify useful fields and acceptance checks.
experiments.treatment: Task, mapping, owner and acceptance example
experiments.guardrail: Scope drift and unnecessary data collection
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

experiments.name: Exception-specific handover
experiments.hypothesis: Operators resolve failures faster when the runbook identifies the failure class.
experiments.treatment: Error class, event key and recovery owner
experiments.primary: Exceptions resolved in a fixed window
experiments.allocation: Use matched account cohorts and a fixed observation window. Review uncertainty and selection effects before expansion.

roadmap.title: Map a customer task
roadmap.body: Observe one customer workflow and document the input, destination, update semantics and success example.

roadmap.title: Ship reliable delivery
roadmap.body: Add event keys, exception routes, bounded retries and representative failure tests.
roadmap.measure: Unique delivery outcomes and unresolved events

roadmap.title: Make handover repeatable
roadmap.body: Document rollout and recovery, collect operator feedback and feed recurring gaps back to product.
roadmap.measure: Operator adoption and repeated failure classes

aiApplication: At Sentrion, I would apply durable pipeline and MCP inspection patterns to signal delivery: validate required fields, retain an event key and classify exceptions. The operating loop would test replay, failure recovery and owner response before broader activation.
